title: How Sam Parr built The Hustle newsletter and how to reach $3M/year solo: math, writing, growth
summary: Sam Parr explains how he went from HustleCon conferences to a daily newsletter that reached ~2M readers and sold to HubSpot. He covers the audience-value math (CPM, niche, B2B), copywriting practice with AIDA, early Reddit/blog growth, selling ads, and why risk-derisking and confidence matter.

principles.text: Learn writing through daily copy work: hand-copy great writing, keep a swipe file, then apply it to real sends.
principles.quote: I would spend an hour every day word for word writing it by hand and that's how I learned how to do it.

principles.text: Use the AIDA framework (attention, interest, desire, action) for everything you write or sell.
principles.quote: I like ADA, attention, interest, desire, action. Uh and that's like a way better format.

principles.text: Before choosing a newsletter niche, do the math: subscribers x sends per month x CPM. Niche and buyer spending power matter more than passion.
principles.quote: one makes two grand a month, one makes $1.2 million a month.

principles.text: Newsletter value is audience size times engagement/influence times the price of what they buy; B2B beats consumer.
principles.quote: number of people multiplied by how engaged they are... Multiplied by uh uh the price of the product.

principles.text: Write like a friend to one reader; personal tone builds the loyalty that makes ads sell.
principles.quote: The cool thing about a newsletter is you write it as if it's just me writing to you, not me to millions of people.

principles.text: Grow by going where your exact target reader already hangs out, with headline-first long-form content, and keep advertisers whole to drive repeat buyers.
principles.quote: with the advertising business as well as any other business, repeat customers is key.
